CA_UTI.title: Catheter-associated urine infection (infection linked to a urine tube)

items: A catheter-associated urinary tract infection is an infection that comes from a urine tube (catheter) in the bladder.
Germs can travel up the tube or along it.
New fever, shivering (rigors), confusion, or feeling unwell with no other cause.
Pain in the back or flank, or blood in the urine.
Urine culture from a newly placed catheter or a fresh sample.
Blood cultures if you are very unwell.
Your doctor will choose antibiotics based on the culture.
If the catheter is no longer needed, your team may remove it.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Keep the catheter tube free of kinks, and tell your nurse about any change.
Tell your nurse or doctor about any new symptoms.
Your team will review whether the catheter is still needed.
Do not have urine tested just because the urine looks cloudy or smells strong; this alone is not a reason for a test.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Fever with shivering, or new confusion
Low blood pressure, dizziness, or fainting
Back or flank pain with feeling very unwell
